message.text:
Add rate limiting and lockout to POST /public/unlock in the NestJS backend "Portail de Depot de Pieces". @nestjs/throttler is already installed but not wired to this route.

1. GLOBAL IP-BASED THROTTLE
Apply @Throttle() at the controller method level on the unlock endpoint specifically (not globally — status/browsing public routes shouldn't be throttled the same way). Reasonable limit: 5 attempts per 60 seconds per IP, using the default ThrottlerGuard behavior.

2. PER-TOKEN LOCKOUT (in addition to IP throttling, not instead of)
Track failed PIN attempts against a specific publicToken, not just IP — an attacker can rotate IPs but not the token they're targeting against a single victim's link.
- After 5 failed attempts against the same token within a rolling 15-minute window, lock that specific link out.
- On lockout, return the exact same generic UnauthorizedException/message already used for a normal wrong-PIN case — do not reveal that a lockout specifically triggered, keep the response indistinguishable so an attacker gets no signal they've been detected.
- Implement with a simple in-memory Map<token, {count, firstAttemptAt}> scoped to PublicService — no Redis needed at this scale. Add a code comment documenting this as a known limitation (resets on app restart, not shared across replicas — acceptable for this single-instance deployment).
- Reset the counter for a token on successful unlock.
- Keep the existing pin_verification_failures_total Prometheus increment as-is — this lockout gives the already-configured HighPinFailureRate alert real teeth (attempts now actually get blocked past threshold, not just observed).

3. TEST
Add a Jest test: 5 failed attempts against the same token, then a 6th attempt with the CORRECT pin is still rejected (proves real blocking, not just counting) with the same generic error message as a normal wrong-PIN case.

CONSTRAINTS
- Don't lock out by IP alone for the per-token mechanism — shared networks (office, school) can have multiple legitimate users on one IP.
- Both mechanisms are complementary, keep both, don't merge them into one.
- Hardcoded reasonable defaults (5 attempts / 15 min) are fine — don't over-engineer configurability via env vars for this scope.

OUTPUT
List which files changed and why, no full file dumps unless I ask.
